newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Eight Burmese drown while fleeing to Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Eight Burmese drown while fleeing to Bangladesh.

text.p: Eight Burmese Moslems were feared drowned when crossing a swirling border river in an attempt to reach Bangladesh, police said on Wednesday.

They said Bangladeshi border guards recovered three bodies but five were still missing after a boat carrying 12 "Rohingya" Moslems from Buthidaung area of Burma's western Arakan province sank in the Naf river early on Tuesday.
"The accident occurred apparently because of heavy load on the small boat ferrying the Rohingyas to Bangladesh to join thousands of other illegal entrants," one police officer said.
"There had been strong current in the river and wind was blowing," he said.

The guards rescued four other Rohingyas near Teknaf town in Cox's Bazar district and sent them to a nearby police station, police said. The two boatmen managed to swim back to the Burmese shore, they said without giving further details.
Bangladesh reported a fresh influx of Burmese Moslems Earlier this week that the Rohingyas said was set off by a growing food shortage, unemployment and forced labour in Arakan.
"Some 20 to 30 families sneak in each night," said one police officer in Cox's Bazar, which borders Arakan.
"At least 5,000 Burmese Moslems...have entered Bangladesh in the last one month," he said on Monday.
The new influx began while some 21,500 Burmese Rohingyas were still huddled in two large camps, awaiting to return home after the long-running process was disrupted on May 1, officials said.

The officials blamed the suspension on delays by Burmese immigration authorities in giving clearance for the home-bound Rohingyas. More than 250,000 Moslems fled to southeastern Bangladesh in early 1992 from Burma's Moslem-majority Arakan province, complaining of military persecution.
Repatriation, supervised the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, began in September that year following an agreement between Dhaka and Rangoon.
Police in Cox's Bazar said that as of Sunday, some 500 Rohingyas had been pushed back in two weeks while trying to enter Bangladesh.
